#3791. Skyrim lead designer hopes Sentinel will finally solve The Elder Scrolls' ladder problem

For such a simple, straightforward real-world object, ladders have been the bane of game developers' existence since the early days of the industry. And Bethesda's The Elder Scrolls Series is certainly no stranger to that struggle.

While we may be years away from the release of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, the recent title reveal reignited conversations about what longtime fans hope to see from it. That includes former Bethesda developers, such as Skyrim lead designer and Bethesda veteran Bruce Nesmith, who picked ladders as one thing he hopes Sentinel actually figures out.

If you're unfamiliar, ladders in Skyrim work in a weird way. You don't animatedly climb up and down them, but rather the character simply teleports from one end to the other. Speaking to The Examined Game (via GamesRadar+), Nesmith said that Skyrim's approach "really limits the art team in terms of how you can do multi-layer [levels]".

"It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders," said Nesmith. "All the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof, you're at the top or you have to climb a stair.

"But to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'You give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' And you know, that caused problems right there."

Nesmith then pointed out the hidden complexity of creating functioning ladders in games, and the scenarios developers have to anticipate and account for, especially in a game as dynamic as an Elder Scrolls title.

"So, I'm halfway up a ladder, and [an] NPC decides to climb down it. What happens?" Nesmith posited. "The NPC has to have AI that will adjust for that. Does the player go through the NPC? Is he blocked by the NPC? Does the NPC stay on the ladder? Does the NPC go back up and know to wait and then come back down?

"And I'm just scratching the surface of some of the problems they brought up. So, it seems simple, and other games have climbing ladders, but we chose to put our efforts into other things to make them better rather than deal with that. So, I'd like to see Bethesda finally come around to making ladders a reality where you're actually climbing them and make the world feel a little more immersive."

While we know very little about Sentinel right now - much less how it's going to solve the ladder problem -that hasn't stopped fans from speculating about a number of topics, including what they believe is going to be a split / alternate timeline setup.

#3790. Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's important because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history."

Perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

While it was known that The Bachelor – ABC’s long-running reality dating show – would return for a 30th season, updates had been scant up until this week. Fans now know that the show is officially set to return in early 2027 and that this season will be headlined by none other than Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman. Bringing an NFL player is a major move on the producers’ parts, to say the least. Now, unsurprisingly, viewers are sharing their thoughts or, more specifically, they’re dropping all kinds of jokes.

This is a major development for the Bachelor franchise, since the massive IP has been relatively dormant amid the 2026 TV schedule following an eventful 2025. Hartman’s inclusion seems to be turning that around in a big way, as more than a few users took to X to respond directly under the show’s official announcement. What’s really making me chuckle is the sheer number of sports-related quips that people seem to be dishing out in response to the news. Check out just a handful of the comments down below:

Honestly, the Internet really understood the assignment when it came to weighing in on this big news. In addition to the sports-centric barbs, though, some seem to be expressing a bit of bewilderment over Hartman being tapped as the lead. There’s another interesting constant within this sea of responses, though, as others now seem to be tempted to tune in Bachelor for the first time due to this star selection. Based on the post below (and some others), people are going to be seated for this upcoming season:

@BachelorABC Can’t wait https://t.co/SlocJRJzXPNovember 13, 2026

Sam Hartman, of course, isn’t the first athlete to have ever been the object of people’s affections on Bachelor, as he’s actually the fifth. However, Hartman – who joined the Washington Commanders in 2024 after going undrafted – is the first currently active athlete to ever be on the program. That could indeed bring a fresh spin to the proceedings, and I’m also already wondering if some of Hartman’s teammates may even appear during the season at some point.

If You Miss The Bachelor, I Found A Great Horror Parody, And It’s Streaming For Free

It would be an understatement to say that the Bachelor franchise as a whole could use a bit of jolt after the drama that unfolded earlier this year with The Bachelorette. Former Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Taylor Frankie Paul was set to headline Season 22. However, ABC decided to shelve the already-filmed episodes after 2023 video footage of Paul assaulting ex-boyfriend Dakota Mortensen surfaced. The incident has called into question not only the stability of Bachelorette moving forward but the state of Bachelor Nation as a whole.

On paper, though, Sam Hartman would appear to be a solid choice for this upcoming season of the dating franchise’s flagship show. (I can also see Bachelor Nation having taken serious measures when screening the former Wake Forest and Notre Dame player following the Paul controversy). Based on these social media comments, there seems to be interest amongst the public, and these jokes could indicate that live-tweeting during the season is going to be wild.

The Bachelor Season 30 premieres on March 21 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and will be streamable the next day with a Hulu subscription.

#3788. Nintendo's legendary Kirby designer Masahiro Sakurai weighs in on gen-AI, saying "it has yet to gain my trust" but not to reject it completely

"Doing nothing is probably not the right approach."

Masahiro Sakurai, the designer behind many iconic Nintendo franchises such as Super Smash Bros. and several Kirby titles, has weighed in on the ongoing discussion of generative-AI use in game development.

At an event celebrating the release of his new book - Masahiro Sakurai’s Thoughts on Games - the veteran director told Famitsu he hasn't and currently isn't using the technology to make games, noting that the role of a designer is to generate ideas.

"It has yet to gain my trust," Sakurai said via DeepL machine translation. Regarding graphical use specifically, he added that, "It must not amount to exploitation of any kind," and that "for the time being, we can produce better results by coming up with ideas ourselves".

But Sakurai is wary of rejecting gen-AI completely, saying "making games today is far too difficult", with some games "running at a loss even after selling millions of copies". A company in that position may go under if it does not change its stance on generative-AI, he suggested. "Doing nothing is probably not the right approach," he said, but "where and how to use it" is a complex topic with a lot of uncertainties. Sakurai is taking "a slow-paced approach" for now.

Outside of regular industry layoffs, the use of generative-AI in games has been the most controversial topic amongst developers and players. Some argue it's already being used in multiple development disciplines, notably programming and writing code. Others, such as Shigeru Miyamoto, are more sceptical of the technology's capabilities, especially when it comes to the more creative and art-driven parts of game development.

#3787. Cover your robot body in magical fungus aplenty and galavant across a mystical, Soulslike world in MycoRelic, now out in 1.0

Robot, robot, robot, robot, mushroom! Mushroom!

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

#3785. Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at

Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

"It's a guilt by association pattern that all developers need to push back on"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney has been in a bit of a one-sided beef with Valve co-founder and CEO Gabe Newell for a while now, lately about Steam's AI disclosure that requires developers to include a label informing Steam users of AI-generated content. Sweeney has had a number of complaints about Valve's storefront over the years, which makes sense as he owns one of its main competitors, the Epic Games Store, but he's been doubling and tripling down on the AI disclosure issue as of late. In a new interview, he not only sharply rebukes the AI label, but embraces AI in game development to degree rarely seen by him or other industry leaders.

Talking to GamesBeat, Sweeney gives one of the most bullish takes on AI generation in games I've seen in my many years covering this topic. Get on-board or die, is essentially his perspective.

"It's really clear to me that large-scale game developers–setting aside indies, where there's always going to be specialties and niches, large-scale game development will be totally changed by AI," Sweeney says. "Teams that don't adopt it will absolutely be left behind and rendered uneconomical, non-viable compared to their peers."

Sweeney says he's against any kind of legislation to curb the use of AI in game development in the US because it would give other countries the advantage. "Everyone is going to be adopting it," he says. "When one team can make a game four times more efficiently – 10 times more efficiently soon, perhaps – than another team can make the same game, there's just no possibility of competing the old way. No game developer has 75% to 95% profit margins that they can put at risk by not being as productive as possible."

There has been massive backlash to AI in games from players, voice actors, artists, and indie developers, but messaging from big studios and publishers generally ranges from cautiously optimistic to vocally and enthusiastically supportive. Meanwhile, a report from GDC found that 55% of respondents said AI was having a negative impact on the industry. Still, Sweeney wants to make sure companies aren't being bullied into choosing human workers over AI.

"Because there's a big resistance movement against AI that seems concentrated on trying to bully developers into not adopting it by attacking individuals, by review-bombing projects and so on, I've been trying to make my views known to as many game developers as possible," he says. "We have to power through this and build awesome games, use maximum acceleration, because it is a survival issue for all the companies in the industry."

Sweeney has called Valve's AI policy "abhorrent," politically motivated, and nonsensical among other things, and we can add another descriptor to the pile today: toxic. When GamesBeat pushes back and suggests Steam's AI label is there to inform players, Sweeney says he doesn't "buy it in the slightest," pointing to Steam's user review system as a means to let players know about "a game's quality, scope, entertainment value and so on." Ultimately, he says AI can be a force for good and bad in game development, and he sees Valve's mandatory disclosure as a judgment on the technology as a whole.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

"You can build good games and bad games without AI. You can build good games and bad games with AI. You can repeat those distinctions for all engines, all development tools, all methodologies, all countries of origin, all teams and so on," says Sweeney. "If we were to identify AI as associated with bad games, that's just unfair to developers who use AI to make good games. It's a guilt by association pattern that all developers need to push back on."

Sweeney argues that Steam's AI disclosure is "being used toxically here, because it's absolutely being used by anti-AI advocates to undermine the reputations of developers and the viability of their projects."

Newell himself has yet to respond to Sweeney's many tirades, but prominent former Valve developer Chet Faliszek hit back in a YouTube video in which he called Sweeney's behavior "AI psychosis." Faliszek also argued that Sweeney was "treating all the players like children" and advised him to "act as a player yourself for a moment and go, 'What would I want to know about a game?'"

Why so many game developers don't want to use generative AI

#3783. Wolfenstein 3 and new id Software game confirmed, as Xbox boss somehow unrelatedly shouts about one person soon wielding "capabilities that once required entire nations"

Asha Sharma had a normal one as Xbox turned 25

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

#3782. Activision cracking down on popular Call of Duty: Warzone app that basically constituted cheating

"Lobby shopping" is what Call of Duty: Warzone players have been calling the ability to check the skill level of players in a lobby prior to joining it, enabling them to pass on those that include a lot of tough competition.

There are several ways players, notably Twitch streamers and content creators, have been able to do that over the years. But the use of one app in particular - Warzone Agent - has been considered by many to be cheating, and Activision is finally doing something about it.

Alongside the launch of Modern Warfare 4's version of Warzone and the game's first season of post-launch content, Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet has announced it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

"Yesterday, we began taking action against Warzone Agent, a paid, unauthorised third party tool that lets users lobby shop in Warzone," the developer revealed in a post on X. "Ricochet anti-cheat will block players attempting to load the software and instruct them to unload it before accessing multiplayer."

Having the ability to cherrypick the lobby with the lowest-skilled players possible bypasses the game's matchmaking algorithm, potentially ruining the game for the dozens of other players in the match. Historically, content creators have used the app (and other methods) to post impressive kill records.

The developer added in a follow-up message that: "Using unauthorised software to manipulate the player experience violates Activision terms of use and leaves your account and hardware subject to enforcement." The language seems to stop just short of outright confirming those players using Warzone Agent will be banned.

As part of this crackdown, Ricochet reiterated its stance on boosting - artificially increasing (or decreasing) one's skill rating - saying that it too is considered cheating. "Receiving a boost, having another player log in to boost your account, or purchasing a boosted account are all against policy," the developer said.

"Boosting services flood lobbies with low effort accounts used to farm XP and complete challenges. Those accounts can later be sold as Ranked Play ready, directly feeding the cheating marketplace."

More than 20,000 boosting-related accounts have been removed since the launch of Modern Warfare 4, according to the developer, and Ricochet will "continue to apply pressure" in this area.

The quality of multiplayer was a particular highlight in Eurogamer's review of Modern Warfare 4, in which Dom Peppiatt lauded the complexity of weapon handling, which works without taking away from accessibility of the gunplay.

The first Despicable Me movie premiered back in 2010, and ever since then Gru and (perhaps more importantly) the Minions have become mainstays of popular culture. I have to admit that I haven't really been a fan of the Illumination franchise, although I do love what the studio did with the Super Mario Bros. movies. Still, when Minions & Monsters arrived on streaming with a Peacock subscription, I tuned in at the behest of my fiancé. And I was shocked by how much I truly enjoyed this latest installment of the animated franchise.

Minions & Monsters reviews were rather positive upon the movie's release, and it's currently sitting at an impressive 89% on Rotten Tomatoes. I had to judge for myself, and I'll admit that those little yellow guys and their lines in Minionese did crack me up. Although I was even more impressed by how the animated family film was connected to the greater moviemaking industry.

Rather than showing the Minions serving Gru, the new movie provide provided them with an origin story. The audience learns that a tribe of the yellow creatures dated back thousands of years ago. We watch as they accidentally kill various evil bosses they have through the years, until eventually the stumble on a bank robbery.

After trying to pledge their loyalty to the robber, both the Minions (and myself) are shocked to learn that they were actually on a film set and the bank heist was nothing but a scene. The studio ends up hiring the Minions (particularly James) when two execs find them amusing, starting an entire career in both silent and talkie films. This is when I really fell in love with Minions & Monsters, which ended up being a love letter to Hollywood.

Some movie lovers wish they had Minions & Monsters as a kid, thanks to how surprisingly rich it was regarding movie history. Indeed, the movie's brisk 90-minute runtime had plenty of great references to classic films. First we're shown a movie museum, where there are nods to The Matrix and E.T. The Extra Terrestrial. George Lucas himself even gets a cameo, although I was waiting for some Star Wars jokes that never happened. Throughout the story we also get references to silent films like like 1878's The Horse in Motion (which was also included in Jordan Peele's Nope), as well as 1896's Train Pulling Into a Station.

When the Minions are working for a Wizard he clearly resembles a similar character from Disney's Fantasia. And once we go from silent films to talkies, one can't help but think about Singin' in the Rain. There's also a shot for shot remake of a scene from Citizen Kane, as well as a hilarious "play it again" reference from Casablanca. There are even nods to modern movies like Damien Chazelle's 2022 flick Babylon. That's just a handful of the movie references packed into Minions & Monsters.

Minions & Monsters is streaming now on Peacock as part of the 2026 movie release list. It's more than possible that the next movie in the Despicable Me franchise won't thrill me like this title did, but I'm definitely more invested in the property than ever before.

#3780. Rockstar's doing a GTA 6 launch 'festival' in Miami featuring a lot of presumably expensive musical stars

The next-level glamour of Grand Theft Auto 6's arrival continues with word that Rockstar is hosting a star-studded launch 'festival' for the game in Miami - the game's setting-by-a-different-name.

The event will feature two stages hosting live performances by musical artists both featured in the game and from those who are not. Cardi B is probably the headliner - my knowledge of popular music is creaking here - but there's also Travis Scott, Don Toliver, Kodak Black, Sofaygo, Ca7riel, and Paco Amoroso.

Meanwhile, GTA 6 soundtrack duo Justice are doing a DJ set, as are The Dare with Fcukers, which is a dangerous name to spell. Also appearing: Metro Boomin, Nick León with DJ Python, Propsa with Skream, Rauw and Friends, Suero, and Tainy.

The event is being hosted at event space Mana Wynwood, and the pre-sale lottery for tickets begins this week on Wednesday, 11th November. Tickets are limited to two a head.

The full soundtrack for GTA 6 is yet to be revealed, with only a handful of songs so far detailed - featuring Rauw, Ca7riel, Paco Amoroso, and Travis Scott, among others. But of course music and radio stations play a huge role in the series, and given the amount of time we'll be playing GTA 6 and listening to these songs, it may well provide a lucrative platform to be featured on.

Meanwhile, the cultural impact of GTA 6's imminent arrival continues with a takeover of swanky department store Selfridges in London, which has a custom Ferrari parked in a window and an extensive range of expensive merch to buy.

It's not all good news for Rockstar, though. The company is also fighting an employment tribunal in Scotland relating to the sudden firing of 31 staff from Rockstar North this time last year. Rockstar alleges this was done for gross misconduct reasons, whereas the fired staff maintain it was done in the name of union busting. The results of that hearing are expected close to GTA 6's release, on 19th November.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Get ready for some wheels within wheels, as DiscussingFilm has revealed an animated trailer for a Grand Theft Auto 6 TV show—and I don't mean a trailer for a show about GTA 6, but a trailer for a show in GTA 6.

Macca and Friends, as the show is known, follows the adventures of a gang of anthropomorphic Floridian—Leonidan, I suppose—animals as they try to find their way in the world, accompanied to some extent by a beefed-up cop. The animals are cops too. It's a bit like Scooby Doo, maybe, but more egalitarian.

Rockstar hasn't said anything about the show, but this isn't the first appearance of Macca: A Macca and Friends mural appeared in a real-life BurgerShot that was set up in Miami's Kaseya Center in October, and a billboard for the show was erected in Miami as well.

Both advertised Macca and Friends as "coming November 19 on Weazel," a Fox-like television channel that exists within the GTA universe.

Rockstar is now marketing GTA 6 with a real-life Burger Shot food stand in Kaseya Center, Miami. They continue preparing for the major Miami Heat event on November 18. (via @nvtnp_) https://t.co/hbAlRKP4A4October 21, 2026

How much of an actual, full-on show Rockstar has constructed here, I cannot say. Remedy has done similar things with its games, but those are just brief snippets delivering a little bit of meta narrative; Rockstar, by comparison, gave us multiple stand-up comedy shows in GTA 5 and black-and-white films in Red Dead Redemption 2… not to mention, fully animated horse testicles. In that light, is it hard to believe they may have created an entire animated series for GTA 6?

It might just be another blast from the GTA marketing machine—Rockstar is also literally renting the Miami Heat to promote its game, after all. At this point I don't think anything's off the table.

PlayStation and Xbox owners will find out in less than a week: Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19. A PC release date (or any kind of PC announcement at all) remains elusive.

#3778. Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!"

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

#3777. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang under investigation after admitting affair with alleged Chinese spy in company-wide email

"There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into its own CEO Jensen Huang, after a report by the New York Times claimed he had been participating in an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Huang admitted to having an affair in a company-wide statement, apologising to his wife as well as to Nvidia employees. Following this acknowledgement, independent investigators are looking into whether or not he's been the target of a "foreign intelligence effort".

Per the New York Times article, the alleged spy was named as Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang or Huang Le. Jensen Huang wrote in his internal letter: "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry."

With regard to security concerns surrounding the CEO of US-based company Nvidia potentially sharing information with a spy, Huang confirmed that the Nvidia board of directors had initiated an investigation. He added: "I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." The Nvidia board has said it has "no reason to believe either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."

Huang will remain CEO of Nvidia while the investigation is conducted. The New York Times report also claimed that US government officials did not believe Huang knew of Alice Huang's alleged intelligence activities for China.

Following the internal letter from Jensen Huang, Nvidia stock took a tumble from $162bn to $150bn. Nvidia, a juggernaut in the video game hardware industry, is also a key player in the global generative AI industry, which is currently carrying the US economy as other sectors struggle. The company is responsible for AI technology like DLSS 5, which generates lighting, shadows and more using generative AI.

Concerns around the Chinese AI sector passing the American industry has been a core argument against AI development slowdown or regulation, and it's also why Huang's affair may be a matter of national interest.

The Marvel Legendary 2nd Edition Core Box improves on the original in nearly every way, delivering what remains one of the best classic deck building systems out there. For Marvel and deck builder fans that may have missed out on the original box, this is an incredibly easy recommendation, but for folks that may just want to replace their old box, you will need to weigh whether the elements here are worth it.

One of the best cooperative deck builders out there

Some great new art and the new neoprene playmat is a nice step up

Includes improvements that were originally added expansions are now included right from the start

Compatible with already released Marvel Legendary products

Did not really improve the storage solution or alleviate setup/teardown hassle

Not as strong value proposition for owners of the original core box

Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

When it comes to the deck building genre of card games, these popular options have featured all manner of different properties and styles over the years, with one of my favorites being Legendary: A Marvel Deck Building Game (henceforth referred simply as Marvel Legendary) from Upper Deck. In fact, this was where I first got my introduction to the deck builder landscape; ever since watching Wil Wheaton's Tabletop episode featuring it, this has been one of my go-to types of games to play.

Now, Upper Deck has released a new edition of the base Marvel Legendary, bringing with it some refinements and updates that the team has picked up in the past 14 years since the original box came out, along with fan-favorite mechanics that were introduced in later expansion content. All of this results in superior, yet still very familiar, new starting point for anyone wanting to assemble some Marvel heroes and save the day – and one of the best card games overall for Marvel fans.

This new 2nd Edition of Marvel Legendary retains the same cooperative deck-building mission as the original, now with a nice neoprene mat gameboard, replacing the classic folding cardboard one. Prior to the game starting, players pick the heroes that they will build their decks with, a total of 15 choices, followed by the villain you will face off against, what their dastardly scheme will be, and the various henchmen and other foes assisting them.

From there, in typical deck-building fashion, over the course of numerous rounds, players will purchase and enhance their decks with hero cards from a shared pool, taking out villains, rescuing captured civilians, and thwarting enough of the mastermind’s schemes and bashing them in the face until either the heroes or villains come out victorious. It’s a tried-and-true formula that has served Upper Deck for many years and many spin-offs, and it all began with Marvel Legendary, and it still is just as fun today.

Players: 1-5Ages: 14+Game type: Deck-buildingComplexity: ModerateLasts: 30-60minsDesigner: Devin LowPublisher: Upper DeckPlay if you enjoy: Gwent, Magic: The Gathering

Legendary adopts a rotating and ever shifting marketplace of cards for folks to pick from, an approach more akin to Ascension as opposed to a static shop like Dominion. It’s an approach I have always favored, and considering all of the new redone art in this box, I appreciated this direction even more, since it lets me see more cards. Having each power of hero card feature its own unique piece of artwork is a great touch, that while fixed in later expansions, was sorely lacking in the original core box. Same with the various schemes you will contend with.

By and large, all the new artwork is an improvement, though some fall a bit flatter, with the “Wound” cards that will clog your deck. Previously, these featured a gruesome image of Wolverine getting blasted, his body contorting with pain as his classic X-men costume is shredded. Now, it’s just Iron Man in pristine looking armor holding his shoulder like he threw a slightly too-fast baseball, and pulled a muscle. I mean, I guess that’s a wound…technically?

For folks that don’t own the original Core Box of Marvel Legendary, this new box is an amazing and spectacular jumping on point for one of the most established deck builders out there. Even if you never touch any of the previously released expansions (that are compatible with this new box, by the way), you still have a fully stocked game that will keep things exciting for years to come. Things become slightly more complicated if you do already own the older box. At $100 msrp, it’s a hefty price tag for what is basically new artwork, some rebalanced cards, a couple and card types like sidekicks and S.H.I.E.L.D Officer Specialists being included (originally released in expansions).

Hardware nerds unite, sign up to our free tech newsletter for a weekly digest of the hottest new tech, the latest gadgets on the test bench, and much more from the team at GamesRadar+.

Even when it comes to the heroes and villains being offered, there is a good deal of crossover between the two boxes. On the heroes side, Deadpool from the OG box has been swapped out for Miles Morales, and Doc Ock has been added to the Mastermind list to represent the web-head’s rogues gallery, along with some adjustments to the henchmen and villain offerings. Again, all of this is great for new players, it’s just something for returning owners to be aware of before they drop the cash on the new box.

There’s a reason that Marvel Legendary would go on to spawn tons of expansions, and with the Legendary series spinning off to feature other properties like The Matrix, Predator, and now even DC. It’s just a damn good game that has withstood the test of time.

Sure, it can still take a bit to set up and pack up, thanks to all the various little decks of cards you need to shuffle together, but the end result has always been worth the hassle. I look at my dinged up, faded, and scratched original core box sitting on my game shelf and remember back to all the fun game nights that it’s been a part of, and this new 2nd Edition Core Box will let the sweet prince finally rest. It’s served its time, and I can’t wait for the future game nights this new box will make.

✅ You like deck building games and don’t have the original core box: If you're a fan of the genre, you owe it to yourself to try this.✅ You're looking for a thematic cooperative game: Want something memorable to bring to your next game night? This is it.

❌ You already own the original box: You will need to weigh whether or not the new art and rebalanced cards are worth the price tag.❌ You prefer your deck building games to be purely competitive: Marvel is full of teams, so it's no surprise this spin-off follows the same formula.

This review was conducted using a sample provided by the publisher. For more details on our process, check how we test board games or the GamesRadar+ reviews policy.

#3775. Anticipated Warhammer 40K tactical RPG Dark Heresy gets a release date

Owlcat Games has revealed a release date for its tactical role-playing sequel Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy. The game arrives 28th January, 2027 on PC, PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X. A Switch 2 release date will be provided "at a later date", a press release says.

Warhammer 40,000: Dark Heresy follows the good work laid down by Warhammer 40,000: Rogue Trader a couple of years ago. "Rogue Trader nails the 40k setting and provides an appropriately massive narrative filled with meaty tactical combat, though some bugs and poor performance hold it back," wrote Caeyln Ellis in Eurogamer's Warhammer 40,000 Rogue Trade review.

Dark Heresy changes things by casting you as an Inquisitor and tasking you with hunting down heretics and purging the world of dark influences, as one is wont to do in the 41st century, it seems. And developer Owlcat has apparently overhauled many of the systems underpinning the adventure.

There's a beta that's been running for a while that offers a complete first Act to try, and it's accessible if you buy a Founders edition of the game. This beta, incidentally, disappears 7th January, when Owlcat prepares the game for launch.

Meanwhile, Owlcat is making a substantially different RPG based around the popular Expanse license - a game that's much more closely inspired by Mass Effect. That project recently recruited the help of former Dragon Age writer David Gaider, and it will no doubt hope to fill a much-lamented hole created recently by the cancellation of Mass Effect 5.

They're like gorgeous Mickey Mouse ears, though.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Fan-favorite fashionista Florence Pugh is back again with another show-stopping ensemble. From sparking the “Free the Nipple” movement with her sheer Valentino dress to making deltoids interesting again, she's now going all method dress for her 2026 Netflix TV release of East of Eden. But if you’re all about stylish ensembles worth talking about, Pugh caught my eye with a black dress with sleeves that resembled (fabulous) Mickey Mouse ears.

Clearly inspired by East of Eden, Florence Pugh has been going all in on the Victorian vibes for the period series' promotional events. Next in line for the Marvel star’s method dressing look, she’s decided to fashion a beautiful black dress at the L.A. FYC event for the show, with those Mickey Mouse ear-like sleeves, and I still can’t take my eyes off them:

From Reed’s spring 2027 collection, the Oscar nominee wore a button-down, tight-fitting black silk dress that’s bringing all kinds of Victorian vibes. To call it timeless would be an understatement.

Still, it's so hard to get over those sleeves! Some may say that they’re like wings, but just take a closer look and you'll see what I mean about the Mickey Mouse ear comparison. They’re so big that they’re as high as her head. Pugh's character, Cathy, wasn’t a woman to mess with, and fittingly, this whole ensemble is giving me the impression that the star herself means business.

As usual, I always have to give Florence Pugh credit for her commitment to making a fashion splash compared and not playing it safe. There’s something theatrical about the whole look, and those sleeves don’t lie. Also, please don't mistake my Mickey comments for shade of any kind. This Disney fan loves those sleeves, and I wish others would take a cue from Pugh.

As previously alluded to, this isn't the first time Pugh has channeled the Victorian age for East of Eden events. She first took the era’s romantic angle at a photo call, wearing a ruffled top with a skirt silhouette that looks like something straight out of the 1800s. Then, at the historical drama’s New York premiere, the Little Women actress fashioned an out-there, stunning corset that also came with voluminous sleeves that were the talk of the internet.

But if we really want to talk about big ruffled shoulders, Pugh was recently on the cover of Elle’s Women in Hollywood issue, donning a perfectly pink East of Eden dress that was ruffled from her shoulders to her toes. If audiences want to learn all about how the ladies of the Victorian era struck a pose, leave it to Pugh to show us how it’s done.

While I would never have expected Florence Pugh to grace us with her presence wearing a black dress resembling Mickey Mouse ears, I think a new trend may be born. If anything, I'm now going to rethink my rankings of Pugh's outfits from the past few weeks.

You can watch her stellar performance in East of Eden in the meantime, as it's streaming with a Netflix subscription. And speaking of Mickey and Disney, catch Pugh in the Disney-produced Avengers: Doomsday, which hits theaters on December 18 amid the 2026 movie schedule.

Just your average South Floridian cinephile who believes the pen is mightier than the sword.

Microsoft has issued an apology for the global services outage that began on November 12, which disrupted access to Microsoft 365 products for governments, hospitals, schools, and businesses around the world. The corporation says that neither AI nor malicious actors were at fault, but that the outage occurred as a result of an underlying infrastructural issue introduced during a network upgrade.

"We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously," Microsoft said. "We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services."

We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions. Given the scale of demand, we restored services gradually, validating stability at each stage. While this took longer, it helped ensure a stable restoration. We will provide a full post-incident report once our review is complete.November 13, 2026

While popular speculation has been eager to attribute the outage to vibe-coding—and I can't blame anyone for speculating, considering Microsoft's push for company-wide AI adoption—the corporation says the outage was "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." It's unclear whether another word was meant to follow "cyber." I'm just telling you what the company wrote.

"The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change," Microsoft said, casually brutalizing the syntax of causality. "We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions."

Microsoft acknowledged that the restoration of service was slower than many might have hoped, but said that it brought services back online gradually to ensure stability.

Even if AI wasn't to blame for this week's outage, it's tempting to wonder whether any of the 10,000 employees Microsoft laid off in 2023 as part of its ongoing cost-cutting strategy might have known how to avoid the costly hiccup. Or any of the 6,000 employees it laid off in May 2025. Or the 9,000 it laid off that July. Or the 4,800 it laid off a year later, including 1,600 at Xbox with another 1,600 to follow. Or the 60,000 employees it extended voluntary buyout offers to last month.

Ah, well. No way to know. Microsoft said it will provide a more detailed incident report once its internal review of the outage is complete.

#3772. Hollow Knight Silksong physical editions mention multiple "free content packs" incoming, and call Sea of Sorrow a "giant expansion"

More than a year after its initial release, physical versions of Hollow Knight: Silksong are finally arriving on players' doorsteps. It's the same brilliant and sometimes thrillingly cruel Metroidvania Eurogamer gave five stars to, except this time a pack-in booklet seemingly reveals the existence of multiple "free content packs" alongside the Sea of Sorrow DLC.

Hollow Knight: Silksong's physical editions were originally set to be delivered from 10th November, but some early handovers have given us a peek inside the box. Redditor Me_975 posted pictures of their Nintendo Switch 2 Edition, and there's a few interesting tidbits tucked away - most notably in the manual's chapter on Content Packs.

"The world of Hollow Knight: Silksong will expand with free content packs," the booklet reads. "Prepare for even more adventures filled with new friends, new abilities, and new ferocious foes!"

Developer Team Cherry confirmed plans for post-launch Silksong support last year, but remained pretty tight-lipped about what exactly that would look like. The indie outfit then announced the nautically themed Sea of Sorrow expansion, though we now have proper confirmation there's more content packs still to come, which shouldn't be a huge shocker considering all the free post-launch love Hollow Knight (the first one) received.

Speaking of Sea of Sorrow, that's mentioned here too: "In the first giant expansion, voyage across and beneath a salt-stricken ocean brimming with mystery and menace."

Sea of Sorrow's original release window was a vague 2026 - time's a-ticking, Team Cherry. Still no release date so far, but the booklet does say it's "Coming Soon." Of course, Team Cherry are quite infamous for working on games until they balloon wildly out of control. After all, Silksong was once upon a time intended to be a Hollow Knight DLC, but with games this detailed, I can't really complain about waiting a little extra.

If you are interested in owning Silksong physically, it comes with a big map of Pharloom and the rest of the booklet also includes some really lovely art seemingly ripped straight from the game, as well.

#3771. Microsoft suffer system outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, exec says there's "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity"

Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

That latest update was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of issues.

"We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity."

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there currently looks to have been no big hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

#3770. God of War: Ragnarok is reportedly the highest-earning PlayStation Studios game this generation, but Marvel's Spider-Man 2 isn't far behind

God of War: Ragnarok is the generation's best-selling and highest-earning PlayStation Studios game, according to a new report, but the full top 10 list has a few nice surprises.

In the four years since its PS5 release and two years since its PC port, God of War: Ragnarok has reportedly sold just over 20m copies and generated $1.4b in revenue, according to estimates from Alinea Analytics. About 27.5 percent of the 15m copies it sold on console came from physical editions, and the action blockbuster apparently sold a further 1.1m this year alone. Not bad, boy.

Those stats should bode well for the series' next romp God of War: Laufey - which sees Faye take the spotlight across a multi-mythological afterlife and was recently delayed into May 2027 - even if PlayStation moves away from PC ports for its signature single-player games.

Kratos and Atreus only narrowly beat out perhaps the biggest superhero of them all: Marvel's Spider-Man 2, a game that reportedly made a whopping $1.3b off 19.1m copies across PS5 and PC. The Spidey sequel should keep swinging even higher as the years chug on, though - the report states that sales always surge during the holiday months, and this year's big screen behemoth Spider-Man: Brand New Day led to an even bigger spike than usual.

Racing sim royalty Gran Turismo 7 ($841m), bug-squashing phenomenon Helldivers 2 ($786m), robo-dino sequel Horizon: Forbidden West ($485m), vengeful spirit sim Ghost of Yotei ($410m), undead remake The Last of Us Part 1 ($341m), multidimensional romp Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart ($334m), Stellar Blade ($316m) and delightful throwback Astro Bot ($292m) round out the top 10 games published by PlayStation Studios this generation.

It's worth noting that Helldivers 2 and Stellar Blade were developed by studios outside the PlayStation umbrella, but the console maker still published both upon release. Ghost of Yotei's performance is also particularly impressive since Sucker Punch's sequel has only been out for a year and didn't get the benefit of a PC port, like many of its PS5 siblings. The success couldn't save Sucker Punch from recent layoffs, however.

On PlayStation's decision to kill disc-based physical releases, analyst Rhys Elliott said that the bottom five games in the list together made $281.7m this year alone: "PlayStation wants those numbers to be bigger in the coming years, which is one of the reasons it's killing the disc (alongside the better margins it and publishers get through digital.)"

Warning! Spoilers ahead for Law & Order: SVU’s 600th episode, “Obedience,” streaming now with a Peacock subscription.

Law & Order: SVU’s reign on television continues, as the 2026 TV schedule plays host to its 28th season. This past week, the series officially celebrated its 600th episode, and that is certainly a rare feat. Unsurprisingly, SVU went all out with the milestone episode by reuniting Mariska Hargitay's Olivia Benson and Christopher Meloni's Elliot Stabler once again. Their reunion stressed me out, and I’m wondering when we’ll see Christopher Meloni again, especially after hearing comments from the showrunner.

In the episode, “Obedience,” Benson has to wrangle in Stabler after one of their first cases from nearly 30 years ago comes back to the surface. It proves to be a difficult situation for the pair, and not because of the nature of the case itself. Apparently, Bensler’s relationship is a bit tense, as up to that point, Benson hadn’t heard from Stabler since Cragen’s memorial at the beginning of SVU Season 27. They had some tough conversations about who they were back in the day and who they are now, and the dynamics between the two are quite surreal.

Showrunner Michele Fazekas recently told TVLine that a lot was said between the fan-favorite duo that needed to happen, even if may lead them on a path that fans aren’t going to like. Fazekas explained:

I actually think this was a cathartic episode for them and that they got to say things that have been lingering that, had they not said it, it wouldn’t have been real. It wouldn’t have been authentic. I love when two people who obviously love each other can hash out their issues like that. It has to happen.

Since the very beginning of SVU, fans have been rooting for Benson and Stabler to become a couple. There have been a few times where it seemed like it could happen, and they have opened up about their feelings for one another. However, based on their reunion in the 600th episode, it was like they were heading in a completely different direction relationship-wise.

Even though Bensler was able to solve the case together, their partnership felt somewhat cold, and I wanted more than anything for them to make up and be best friends again. That being said, Fazekas defended the decision, and I can admittedly see why:

Because I do think they end in a lovely place. But listen: I find, when you’re writing anything, people getting along the whole time is fine. But it’s not drama. And it’s not real.

As someone who has been rooting for Bensler for years, I was sad to see how little they’ve been talking, with Stabler basically staying off the grid for months. But of course, friends, even longtime partners, drift apart, and while it’s definitely not what I would have wanted, it’s understandable that Fazekas would want this for them. Besides, fans can look at it as just another obstacle. Of course, there's also the question as to whether Stabler will back back on SVU again this season, and Fazekas said this on that subject:

No, not this season... We’ve told that story. [Stabler] has got his assignment, which is to go work on some stuff. And I think he will.

After closing the case, Benson and Stabler parted ways, with Stabler heading on a trip to Arizona. Stabler did ask Benson to come with, but she couldn’t, noting she has her son, Noah, and wouldn’t be able to leave. They ended on relatively respectful terms after airing some things out, and they seem to be in a good place now. Even though we won’t be seeing Stabler again this season, I have hope that we will see him again sometime down the road. I truly believe another Benson and Stabler reunion is a given, I just don't know how long we'll have to wait.

Even if we don’t see Christopher Meloni again on SVU for a while, fans will still be able to look forward to seeing him on the small screen. After wrapping the first season of The Land earlier this year, Hulu announced that the upcoming NFL drama will premiere on February 17, 2027. So that’s definitely a plus. For now, SVU returns for its fall finale on December 3. Catch up on recent episodes now by heading to Peacock.

Now that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's latest remake is out in the wild, all eyes have turned to a certain smiling moon up above. But while fans speculate about the series' future, two former Nintendo marketing leads reckon a Majora's Mask remake is almost definitely on the way.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's Switch 2 revival sold in droves earlier this month, moving more than 5 million copies in its first four days and leading to speculation about what comes next. For Kit Ellis and Krysta Yang (Nintendo of America's former marketing and PR leads), the series' future doesn't look so different to its past.

Speaking in the most recent episode of the Kit and Krysta podcast, the duo wonder if it's now a "foregone conclusion" that Nintendo will also remake Majora's Mask in the same style as Ocarina of Time's 2026 re-up. "I still think yes," Yang says. "They couldn't have been on the fence because they probably already started making it. I don't see why you wouldn't."

Nintendo pulled the same trick almost three decades ago when Majora's Mask came out less than two years after Ocarina of Time on the N64, which is almost unfathomable with how long 2026 development cycles can be. (Th two 3DS remakes also launched with little time in-between.) But Nintendo was able to pull it off because Majora's Mask smartly reused many of the assets, character models and systems that had already been built for Ocarina of Time - a feat it might be able to repeat once again.

"It may not be the next game," Ellis continues. "It may not be in the next one to two years, but so much of the foundational work has been done and it's the same work that let them make the original Majora's Mask very quickly after the original Ocarina on Nintendo 64… The ceiling has not yet been realized on Majora's Mask."

The duo also speculate that if Nintendo wants to release a Zelda game every year, it'll likely rotate between new 2D entries, new 3D ones, and remakes. A Majora's Mask remake built off of the Switch 2's Ocarina of Time seems like an easy decision.

"It just doesn't make sense for them not to do it," Yang adds.
